claim: Information-gain (D-optimal) channel selection beats uniform spacing at an equal measurement budget N.
prereg_criteria: Paired per-seed difference d_s = err_infogain(s) - err_uniform(s). A win requires BOTH: the bootstrap 95% CI of the mean of d_s excludes zero (10000 resamples, rng_seed fixed before the run), AND |median(d_s)| exceeds run-to-run variability, defined as the median of the per-arm seed-wise MAD. Registered verdict labels: infogain wins if median(d_s) < 0, uniform wins if median(d_s) > 0, otherwise no difference. A near-miss is not reread as a win.
measured: 20 seeds x 5 budgets x 3 arms = 300 trials, no missing cells. N=5: median(d_s) = +0.0962, CI95 [0.0800, 0.1113], run variability 0.0054 -> uniform wins. N=10: median(d_s) = +0.0142, CI95 [0.0134, 0.0361], run variability 0.0012 -> uniform wins. N=20 and above: no difference. Mean error at N=5 was 0.0719 for uniform against 0.1685 for information gain, i.e. the clever arm was 2.3x worse. Gate check: at N=101 all arms use every channel and their errors agreed, so the harness was not silently differing.
reopen_condition: A prior model whose linearisation point is not fixed before observation. The registered explanation for the loss is that a batch design commits the entire budget on the basis of a prior that turns out to be wrong; a design that does not do this has not been measured here.
source: adaptive-sampling lane of the private system, day-4 arm comparison (pre-registration and result records)

claim: Ordering pending work by estimated expected loss (equivalently, by estimated information gain) beats a simple structural rule.
prereg_criteria: The clever ordering is adopted only if (i) it beats a simple structural rule in at least one of the three independent lines where the comparison had already been run, and (ii) the ordering signal has a ground truth outside the estimator's own output. Condition (ii) was registered because the failure mode being guarded against is an estimator whose input is text the same system produced.
measured: 0 of 3 independent lines favoured the clever method; the simple structural rule won in all three. Condition (ii) failed independently: of 18 usable evidence sources, the number carrying an explicit priority, deadline or dependency was 0, so the estimate would have had no external referent at all. The sample size available for the loss numerator was 1, with no interval.
reopen_condition: Measured count of records carrying an explicit priority, deadline or dependency rises above zero, giving the estimator an input it did not generate itself. Until then this is not a tuning problem.
source: task-generation design record of the private system, clever-ordering candidate, plus its source inventory

claim: On Defects4J, a structural test selector achieves higher fault-relevant test recall than a uniform control at an equal budget.
prereg_criteria: Four controls had to hold before any score was reported. C1: the control's selection actually differs from the arm's, counted over the corpus. C2: the control varies with N. C3: the control is capable of winning somewhere. C4: the control is not pinned at the floor or ceiling. The registered stopping rule: if the control is tautological, the run is not scored at all, rather than scored with a caveat.
measured: Corpus 854 bugs across 17 projects, all usable. The first scoring run reported macro recall 0.6131 for the selector against 0.2494 for uniform at N=5, and it passed C1 with 199 bugs selecting differently. Self-audit then found that only the selector arm consumed modified_classes, which is derived from the fix commit and is therefore not available at inspection time. With that input removed, the selector's selection became identical to uniform's: C1 fell to 0 of 854. Under the registered stopping rule the run was not scored, and the earlier positive number was withdrawn rather than reported with a caveat.
withdrawn_claim: macro recall 0.6131 for the selector against 0.2494 for uniform at N=5 on Defects4J
reopen_condition: None. This is a property of the substrate, not a threshold: neither modified_classes nor relevant_tests can be rewound to the information state available at inspection time, so the comparison cannot be made fair on this corpus. The measurement was moved to real repository history instead, which is NR-004. No substitute metric was invented for this one.
source: adaptive-sampling lane, defect-corpus scoring after the leak repair

claim: The selector's recall is a property of the selector, so a recall measured on one repository transfers to another.
prereg_criteria: Each repository is scored independently and results are never pooled, specifically so that a weak repository cannot be hidden inside an average. PASS requires, for every repository: cond1, macro(selector) > macro(uniform) at every budget N; and cond2, the repository's own recall at N=40 is at least 0.50. The floor of 0.50 was fixed before the run and was declared immovable. Temporal rollback was enforced: the selector saw only the non-test files changed by commit C and the test-file listing at C~1, never the labels.
measured: Two repositories, ~290 sampled commits each, pre-check passed on both (selection differed from uniform on 240/293 and 270/286). cond1 held everywhere. cond2 did not: recall at N=40 was 0.1993 on one repository and 0.7869 on the other, a factor of 3.9 apart under an identical selector and an identical protocol. One is below the floor, the other well above it. Verdict FAIL. Two weaknesses are recorded with the result rather than around it: the uniform control never wins anywhere, so cond1 is a low bar and its C3-equivalent fails; and sampling is label-conditioned, since commits that changed no test file cannot have a defined recall and are excluded, so nothing is claimed about them.
withdrawn_claim: that a single measured recall figure characterises the selector
reopen_condition: A control that can win somewhere, plus recall at N=40 at or above 0.50 on every repository scored, with repositories still scored independently. Raising the count of repositories until the mean clears the floor does not satisfy this.
source: adaptive-sampling lane, repository-history corpus (pre-registration and result records)

claim: A predicate-drafting arm can be shown to outperform its controls, so the capability is measurable on the current fixture.
prereg_criteria: Three conditions had to hold before the agreement rate was treated as a result. The one that decided it: every control that could plausibly pass must score below the treatment arm. If a beatable control scores above the arm, the run is not scored and no pass/fail on the capability is issued. The registered reopen threshold for the surrounding programme was a point-estimate interval width of 0.03 or narrower.
measured: Second fixture round. Treatment (drafting) 0.12. Controls: unrelated-by-file-count 0.0, partial-correlation 0.48, neighbourhood 0.0; tautological and contradictory both 0.0 and not counted as controls. 19 independent units against 10 required, 3 distinct classes, 11 unmeasurable. The partial-correlation control scored 0.48 against the treatment's 0.12, so condition three failed and the agreement rate was not scored. Separately the interval width came out at 0.0808 against the required 0.03 (Wilson 95%); closing that gap needs the denominator raised to 234, which the available population does not supply.
withdrawn_claim: that the first fixture round showed the drafting arm at parity with its best control - that round's unrelated-by-file-count control scored 1.0, tying the treatment, which identified it as a degenerate solution rather than a result
reopen_condition: Two things, both required. The interval width must reach 0.03 or narrower, which needs a denominator of 234. And the neighbourhood control's 0.0 must be re-measured on a fixture that injects two defect kinds into the same target - the current fixture injects only one, so that control is structurally incapable of scoring above zero and its 0.0 is a measurement defect rather than a performance result. The failure of condition three stands independently of that defect, because the partial-correlation control alone exceeded the treatment.
source: frozen measurement lane of the private system, second fixture round

claim: The publish gate's self-approval defense establishes that the approving party and the acting party are different.
prereg_criteria: The env-less approval path refuses a record whose creating session equals the session performing the action, and refuses a creating session the checker has never witnessed. The check passes only when both hold. Treat the claim as supported only if satisfying the check requires a second party, not merely a second session.
measured: 2026-08-15. The agent created an approval for an irreversible publish; the check refused it (creating session == acting session), which is the intended behaviour. The agent then started a second session, created the same approval there, and the check passed. Both sessions were the same agent, under the same uid, with write access to the ledger and the session registry. Elapsed time to satisfy the check: one command. The checker's own source documents this as an unclosed residual: an agent with read+write to the ledger can reuse a real prior session id, and closing it requires a signature from an operator-held key.
withdrawn_claim: None. The check was never claimed to do more than this in its source; the gap is between what the check's name suggests and what it establishes.
reopen_condition: Approvals carry a signature verifiable against a key the executing agent cannot read. Then a session boundary is no longer the thing being tested, and the claim can be measured again.
source: publication boundary of the private system, approval ledger and publish gate (approval record and gate output of 2026-08-15)
